title: eng-releases
text:
eng-releases

Amanda: Quick heads-up — I’m planning an autoscale policy migration for the dedicated GPU pools tomorrow 06:30 PDT. This is a config-only change (no runtime code), but it touches slice weights + cooldowns. Need folks for smoke checks and rollback. Plan below.

Raj: 👍 What exactly are we changing?

Amanda: We’re moving from the old static cooldown (120s) and equal slice weights to a tiered weight model and short cooldowns for inference slices used by low-latency routes. Main diffs:
- reduce cooldown from 120s -> 30s for low-latency slices
- add slab_weight for burst slices (0.6) and baseline_weight (0.4)
- canary only on pool gpu-slice-canary

Ben: Can you drop the exact config snippet? I’ll review the k8s ConfigMap patch.

Amanda: Sure — patch we’ll apply via deploy-bot: 

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: gpu-autoscale-policy
  namespace: infra-dedicated
data:
  policy.yaml: |-
    pools:
      - name: gpu-slice-canary
        cooldown: 30
        weights:
          baseline: 0.4
          burst: 0.6
      - name: gpu-slice-prod
        cooldown: 60
        weights:
          baseline: 0.7
          burst: 0.3
```

Sasha: Nice. Any model-serving implications? KV cache TTL stays the same?

Amanda: KV cache TTL unchanged. This only affects how quickly the autoscaler will spin extra slices up/down. We expect transient spike handling to be faster but steady-state cost similar.

Joan: I can own smoke tests. What do you want validated?

Amanda: Thanks Joan — smoke checklist: 
1) Confirm canary pool scales to 2 slices under load.
2) Validate low-latency route latency P50 remains within 10% of baseline.
3) Confirm there are no error spikes in inference logs (500s).
4) Ensure rollout doesn't touch Dedicated capacity reservations.

Joan: I’ll run synthetic ramp: `hey -n 2000 -c 40 http://gpu-slice-canary.internal/api/v1/generate` and attach traces.

Ben: I’ll do the ConfigMap apply and watch for k8s events. Will run `kubectl -n infra-dedicated rollout restart deploy/autoscaler` after patch.

Raj: I can monitor cost signals & console dashboards for unexpected allocation. I’ll keep an eye on token-level unit cost.

Amanda: Rollout plan (sequence):
- 06:30 PDT: pause new user traffic, put non-critical routes to degraded -> route-rule override
- 06:32 PDT: apply canary ConfigMap to gpu-slice-canary
- 06:35–06:50 PDT: Joan runs smoke tests; Ben watches k8s events; Raj watches console metrics
- 06:55 PDT: if canary good -> apply to gpu-slice-prod with staggered rollout (10% of slices every 2m)
- 07:10 PDT: final sanity checks, unpause traffic

Amanda: Rollback plan if anything flaps:
- manual rollback: `kubectl -n infra-dedicated apply -f gpu-autoscale-policy@stable.yaml` (we keep the stable manifest in git tag `autoscale/stable`)
- fallback: switch routing to smaller instance types for latency-critical routes for 5 minutes if autoscaler misbehaves

Sasha: Who’s on rollback?

Ben: I’ll be primary for rollback (apply stable manifest + restart deploy). Raj will be secondary to flip routing if needed.

Joan: I’ll sign off smoke or raise immediate fails. Will post logs to the thread.

deploy-bot: Scheduled config-update job queued: job_id=cfg-2026-1934567890. ETA 06:32 PDT.

Raj: FYI — I set an alert: `autoscale.policy.anomaly` -> slack #incidents + pager for Sev2 if slice churn > 5x baseline in 5m.

Amanda: Perfect. A couple of quick asks:
- Ben, set the job TTL to keep previous ConfigMap for 30m after apply (for easy revert).
- Joan, paste baseline latency numbers in the thread before you start so we can compare.

Ben: Will do. `kubectl apply --record` + keep backup ConfigMap as `gpu-autoscale-policy@pre-1934567890.yaml`.

Joan: Baseline numbers from today: canary P50=34ms, P95=120ms. I’ll attach results after the ramp.

Amanda: Thanks. If anything urgent happens, call out `@oncall` and mark the thread with :rotating_light:. Otherwise I’ll kick at 06:30.

Raj: One more— Are we adjusting any burst budget or just weights?

Amanda: Just weights + cooldowns. No budget changes.

Ben: I’ll post the apply command shortly and the job link.

Joan: Ready on my side. Setting reminder for 06:25 PDT.

Sasha: Good luck team. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Job started: job_id=cfg-2026-1934567890 at 06:32 PDT. Logs: http://ci.internal/jobs/cfg-2026-1934567890/logs

Ben: applied at 06:32:29. `kubectl apply -f gpu-autoscale-policy-canary.yaml` -> success. Watching events.

Joan: Starting synthetic ramp now. First 2 minutes into test — P50 ~36ms, P95 ~130ms, errors 0 so far.

Raj: Console shows canary slice count increased from 1 -> 3 during ramp, cost delta within expected range. No anomalous churn.

Amanda: This looks good from my side. Proceeding to staggered prod rollout at 06:55.

Ben: Applying prod in 10% increments. First apply done.

Joan: Prod slice P50 ~35ms, P95 ~125ms, no errors. Will keep running load for 10m.

Raj: No alerts fired. autoscale.policy.anomaly stayed quiet.

Amanda: Excellent. Finalizing unpause at 07:10 PDT. Great coordination — thanks everyone. I’ll create a short release note and tag `autoscale/migrated-1934567890`.

Ben: Backed up pre-change config at git tag `autoscale/stable@pre-1934567890`.

Joan: Uploading smoke logs to the thread artifacts folder.

Sasha: :tada:

deploy-bot: Job completed successfully: job_id=cfg-2026-1934567890. Duration 00:07:12.
